Not intended to offend, but you do not know what you are talking about. Natural Language Understanding (turning the words into meaning and action) is absolutely the hard part, but not in terms of processing power. Processing a text string that is the raw output from the speech conversion is not something that consumes much computer horsepower. Contextual understanding or NLU systems rely heavily on the system knowing something about conversation context... rules like "once he asks me to play music, I listen for song names and artists." Once the system knows the conversation is about music is constrains the matching algorithm to a much smaller word list. It then gets very good at playing the exact song you asked for. This is the skilled installation and configuration I was talking about. You set up a system and teach it how to understand commands related to it's capabilities. If you have a system that can play music and control the lights, you tech it to be really good at understanding those conversations. You only teach it to understand conversations about the temp if you have also hooked it up to the heating system. This is where all the magic is. Products on the market come in three varieties: 1) it sends everything to the cloud and the company builds these rules over time on their systems. 2) You buy something that has predefined logic and is task specific like a thermostat 3) Ultra expensive systems that come with tools for building recognition libraries and conversation trees and/or professional service from the vendor where they will assist in the creation of custom recognition libraries and conversation trees.

For clarity: the things is category three have six figure price tags and really only get bought for business... my point is not about the price or availability... my point is that the hardware to run these things is modest. It is not the hardware issues and computing power required that keep most of these systems int he cloud.
